gen_risks.description: Failure to operationalize and sustain the new LMIS and Employability Portal due to technical complexity and historical adoption challenges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive mapping of existing DTEFP tools, design cloud-based architecture, and partner with private entities to leverage existing job-matching solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: an 'Employment Observatory' was previously developed with support from... ILO but never fully operationalized, and a digital 'Employability Portal'... was conceived but never launched.

gen_risks.description: Inability of public TVET institutions to deliver quality, market-aligned training due to severe resource, infrastructure, and staffing gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish Workforce Development Committees, partially compensate centers based on student targets, and centralize equipment procurement through AFAP.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps, and weak employer participation in curricula design

gen_risks.description: Delays in disbursing sub-grants, stipends, and scholarships to youth and MSME beneficiaries due to non-compliance or fiduciary verification checks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate explicit eligibility and verification criteria in the Project Operations Manual and execute disbursements through a contracted payment service provider.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria.

gen_risks.description: Project implementation delays caused by slow annual workplan preparation and complex approvals across multiple institutional stakeholders.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a Ministerial Coordination Committee to streamline annual workplan reviews and enforce operational timelines established in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable youth, women, and non-capital populations or exposure to elite capture during beneficiary selection for grants and scholarships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Unique Social Registry data for objective socio-economic targeting, enforce a 50% female quota, and implement transparent outreach in underserved areas.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... as well as risks of elite capture in the selection of beneficiaries

gen_risks.description: Risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment (SEA/SH) targeting young women during professional training and internship placements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an AFAP Social Specialist with SEA/SH expertise, enforce strict workplace codes of conduct, and implement a dedicated Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women participating in training and work placements

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and overlapping mandates across MLSSS, MECSHE, MEF, MEYST, and MAFRD hindering cohesive policy execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Unify implementation under a single MLSSS PIU and establish formal cross-ministerial coordination channels under the authority of the Minister of Labor.
gen_risks.evidence: MLSSS holds the primary mandate... MECSHE oversees longer-term... Entrepreneurship support is currently under... MEF... Sectoral ministries... also have a role to play

gen_risks.description: Recurrent natural hazards such as floods, storms, and sea-level rise causing physical damage to facilities and disruptions to training schedules.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient design and EDGE standards in infrastructure construction/rehabilitation, and utilize phased, flexible training schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and climate shocks may cause disruptions in service delivery, potentially leading to short delays

gen_risks.description: Environmental degradation and waste management hazards arising from civil rehabilitation works and construction of the Príncipe training center.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate environmental screening, contractor waste management plans, adherence to ESMP guidelines, and compliance with EDGE green building standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Project activities may result in the generation of solid waste, obsolete equipment, and minor construction debris... in a sensitive island environment.

gen_risks.description: Procurement and execution bottlenecks resulting from delayed technical inputs and specification handovers between MLSSS and AFAP.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated PIU technical specialists within 45-60 days of effectiveness and establish strict TOR submission workflows within the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: A key factor for good procurement performance will be the ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration

gen_risks.description: Frequent electrical outages and connectivity disruptions impairing the continuous operation of digital LMIS tools and the Employability Portal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure backup power generators for system hardware, implement cloud-based platform architecture, and support off-grid solar energy systems.
gen_risks.evidence: specifically intense rainfall and floods which may disrupt electricity access, the project will support the purchase of power generators

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
